talk: A dollar today is worth more than a dollar next year, because today's dollar can be invested or used to pay down debt. Discounting turns future money into today's money so you can compare fairly. The further away the money, the less it's worth now.

terms.meaning: The yearly return you could get elsewhere, used to shrink future money.
What future money is worth today.
The idea that money now beats the same money later.

questions.prompt: A sponsor offers $110,000 paid in one year, or $100,000 today. Your discount rate is 10% a year. What's the $110,000 worth today?
questions.hint: Divide by (1 + the rate) for each year of waiting.
working: The two offers are worth the same. If you'd rather have the cash sooner, take it today.
whyNot: $110,000 x 10% = $11,000, and $110,000 - $11,000 = $99,000 takes 10% off the future amount. Discounting divides by 1 plus the rate instead: $110,000 / (1 + 10%) = $100,000.
$110,000 is what you'd get next year. Money that far away is worth less today.
$110,000 x (1 + 10%) = $121,000 grows the money forward a year. You need to shrink it back to today.

questions.prompt: An agent offers a deal: $1M paid now, or $1.21M paid in two years. At a 10% discount rate, what's the $1.21M worth today?
questions.hint: Two years away, so discount twice.
working: Same value either way. Two years out, $1.21M is only worth $1M today.
whyNot: $1.21M / (1 + 10%) = $1.1M only discounts one year. The money is two years away, so discount twice.
$1.21M is the amount in two years. Today it's worth less.
$1.21M x (1 + 10%) x (1 + 10%) = about $1.46M grows the money two more years. You want to shrink it back to today.

questions.prompt: Refurbishing a stand costs $250,000 today and saves $100,000 at the end of each of the next 3 years. At a 10% discount rate, are the savings worth more than the cost?
questions.hint: Discount each year's saving separately, then add them up.
working: $250,000 - $248,685 = $1,315 short. Close, but it doesn't pay.
whyNot: 3 x $100,000 = $300,000 adds the savings as if they all arrived today. Later money is worth less, so it shrinks to about $249,000.
$300,000 - $250,000 = $50,000 ignores when the savings arrive. Discounted, they fall just short of the cost.
Close, but not exact. The savings are worth $248,685 today, a little under the $250,000 cost.

penalty.prompt: You'll receive {fut} in two years. Your discount rate is {r} a year. What's it worth today?
penalty.hint: Divide by (1 + the rate) once for each year of waiting.
working: {fut} / {1 + r|pct} = {fut / (1 + r)|usd} a year from now.

traps.why: That only discounts one year. The money is two years away.

call.title: The sponsor's two offers
call.prompt: A sponsor offers $500,000 today, or $520,000 paid next season. Your money is worth about 10% a year to you.

options.label: Take $500,000 today
options.result: Good call. $520,000 next season is worth $520,000 / (1 + 10%) = about $472,727 today, less than the $500,000 on the table.

options.label: Wait for $520,000
options.result: $520,000 / (1 + 10%) = about $472,727 in today's money. More dollars, less value.

options.label: Ask for $100,000 a season for six seasons
options.result: More dollars in total, but most of it arrives years away. Discounted at 10% a year, it's worth less than the $500,000 on offer today.

takeaway: Money later is worth less than money now. Shrink it before you compare.
